provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: God cares for us
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state how God cares for them.
The pupils should be able to list things God provides.
Introduction:
Last term we learned about God's love. Today we learn how God cares for us.
Content:
God feeds the birds. He gives them food every day. God cares for me more. He gives me food, clothes, and a home. My parents give me food like rice and beans.
Class activity:
Let's sing 'God cares for me' and clap our hands.
Evaluation questions:
What does God give the birds?
How does God care for you?
Can you name one thing God gives you?
Summary:
God cares for us every day.

topics.title: Praying to God
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain when to pray.
The pupils should be able to recite the Lord's prayer simply.
Introduction:
We learned God cares for us. Today we learn how to talk to God.
Content:
We pray when we wake up. We pray before eating. We pray when we need help. The Lord's prayer is 'Our Father who art in heaven...'. We pray with simple words like 'Thank you God'.
Class activity:
Let's practice praying together. Close your eyes and say 'Thank you God for my food'.
Evaluation questions:
When should we pray?
What do we say in the Lord's prayer?
How do we start our prayer?
Summary:
Praying is talking to God every day.

topics.title: Jesus the good shepherd
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell the story of the good shepherd.
The pupils should be able to explain how Jesus guides us.
Introduction:
We learned about praying. Today we learn about Jesus as our shepherd.
Content:
A shepherd takes care of sheep. Jesus is our good shepherd. He keeps us safe. Jesus guides me like a shepherd guides sheep. When I am lost, Jesus finds me.
Class activity:
Let's play follow the leader. I will be Jesus and you will be the sheep.
Evaluation questions:
Who is the good shepherd?
How does Jesus guide us?
What does a shepherd do for sheep?
Summary:
Jesus is our good shepherd who keeps us safe.

topics.title: Being kind to others
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell the good neighbour story.
The pupils should be able to list kind actions.
Introduction:\>Last term we learned about sharing. Today we learn about being kind.
Content:
The good neighbour story is about helping others. Kind actions include sharing toys, helping friends, and saying nice words. When my friend falls, I help them up.
Class activity:
Let's act out being kind. One pupil will pretend to fall, another will help them up.
Evaluation questions:
Who was the good neighbour?
What kind actions can you do?
How do you feel when someone is kind to you?
Summary:
Being kind makes others happy and pleases God.

topics.title: Saying sorry
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell the story of David saying sorry.
The pupils should be able to explain God forgives us.
Introduction:
We learned about being kind. Today we learn about saying sorry when we do wrong.
Content:
David said sorry to God when he did wrong. God forgave David. When I do wrong, I should say sorry. God forgives me too like my parents forgive me.
Class activity:
Let's practice saying sorry. Look at your friend and say 'I am sorry'.
Evaluation questions:
Who said sorry to God?
What should we do when we do wrong?
Does God forgive us when we say sorry?
Summary:
God forgives us when we say sorry.

topics.title: Giving to others
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why we should share.
The pupils should be able to tell a giving story.
Introduction:
We learned about saying sorry. Today we learn about giving to others.
Content:\>We share our toys and food with others. Giving stories include the widow who gave her last coin. When I give my biscuit to a friend, I make them happy.
Class activity:
Let's bring something small to share with the class next week.
Evaluation questions:
Why should we give to others?
What did the widow give?
What can you share with others?
Summary:
Giving makes others happy and pleases God.

topics.title: Obeying my parents
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell the obedient child story.
The pupils should be able to list blessings of obedience.
Introduction:
We learned about giving. Today we learn about obeying our parents.
Content:
The obedient child listens to parents. Obeying parents brings blessings. When I obey my parents, God is happy. I get good things when I obey.
Class activity:
Let's play 'Simon says' to practice obeying.
Evaluation questions:
Why should we obey our parents?
What happens when we obey?
Who should we obey?
Summary:
Obeying our parents pleases God and brings blessings.

topics.title: God's house
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain going to church.
The pupils should be able to state how to respect God's house.
Introduction:\>We learned about obeying parents. Today we learn about God's house.
Content:
God's house is the church. We go to church to worship God. We respect God's house by sitting quietly, not shouting, and not running inside.
Class activity:
Let's practice walking quietly into the classroom like entering church.
Evaluation questions:
What is God's house?
How do we respect God's house?
Why do we go to church?
Summary:\>We should respect God's house when we go there.

topics.title: Singing to God
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing praise songs.
The pupils should be able to explain why we sing to God.
Introduction:
We learned about God's house. Today we learn about singing to God.
Content:
 praise songs are happy songs to God. We sing to God because He is good. Singing with joy makes our hearts happy.
Class activity:
Let's sing 'Jesus loves me' together with clapping.
Evaluation questions:
Why do we sing to God?
What kind of songs do we sing?
How do you feel when singing to God?
Summary:
We sing happy songs to praise God.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall term lessons.
The pupils should be able to answer questions about songs and stories.
Introduction:
Today we revise all we learned this term and have fun with songs and stories.
Content:
Let's remember about God caring for us, praying, Jesus as shepherd, being kind, saying sorry, giving, obeying, respecting God's house, and singing praise.
Class activity:
Let's play a game where we answer questions about our lessons and sing our favorite songs.
Evaluation questions:
What did we learn about God caring for us?
How do we pray?
Who is our good shepherd?
Summary:
We remember all we learned this term about God and Jesus.
